senses.gloss:
Nātha in Vedic literature appears only as a neuter meaning ‘protection,’ and is of rare occurrence. Generally, too, very little appears in Vedic literature of practices such as those which produced Anglo-Saxon society or the Roman patronatus.
Foot notes Av. iv. 20, 9; ix. 2, 17; xviii. 1, 13; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 6, 4, 1. Also in Av. xiii. 2, 37, nātha-kāma, ‘seeking help’; xi, 1, 15, nātha-vid, ‘finding help’; pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xiv. 11, 23, nātha-vindu, ‘procuring protection,’ as the name of a sāman, or chant.
In the post-Vedic literature, on the other hand, the word is a masculine, meaning ‘protector,’ and is very common.
